# Review — iliad-043 (7.181–282), first pass

Edits were made to `units.json` by script; `t` was never touched (checked: the units' `t`, joined, equal lines 181–282 of the archive; every `ln` is the line the unit starts on; `l` keeps the line division of `t`; `i` has no `\n`). `gloss.json` does not exist yet and was not touched; the second pass over it is still to come. Unit numbers below are by `ln` (the two units at 260 are told apart by "260b" for the second). Severity: HIGH = wrong English or a false statement a reader would be misled by and the validator or house rule would reject; MEDIUM = a grammatical label or house rendering that was wrong; LOW = loose wording, a wrong cross-reference, a note out of step with `l`/`i`, or a required addition.

Checked and found sound (no change): all 5 speeches (Ajax 191–199, the man who prays 202–205, Ajax 226–232, Hector 234–243, Idaeus 279–282): “ on the first unit's `l` and `i`, ” on the last, nothing in between (5 and 5 in each layer), `mark` on the first unit of each; the previous part (iliad-042) ends with the man's prayer closed by ”, and Idaeus' speech ends inside this part. `p` on the five ¶ units (181, 200, 206, 233, 244). Whole-unit repeats keep the published English exactly: 7.201 (= iliad-042, 7.178), 7.202 first half (3.276), 7.229–230 (2.771–772, cut at λαῶν), 7.251–252 (3.357–358), 7.253 (3.359 + ἔγχος), 7.254b (3.360); the first line of 7.244 and 7.250 (3.355–356) and 7.257 match iliad-019 and iliad-034 word for word; 7.245 and 7.266 (same Greek) have the same English. Units end at ano teleia, or at a comma only where the sentence would run past four lines (7.222 and 7.260b, both justified). Cross-references checked: 3.276, 3.348, 3.355–360, 2.771–772, 5.782–783, 5.245, 5.289, 2.578, 7.39, 7.178, 7.194, 7.196, 7.220, 7.223, 7.245, 7.267, 9.538 and the previous part's "nine" and "two Ajaxes" are true (exceptions below). Every claim about where a word stands (line ends, "next line", "the start of line 211") was checked against the lines.

## Findings considered and refused

- **7.241 `i` "dance the dance of hostile war".** A cognate accusative the Greek lacks, and possibly a remembered phrase, but no source can be named and the sentence rebuilds from μέλπεσθαι "dance" + Ἄρηϊ + σταδίῃ as new-renderings records. Left, flagged below.
- **7.197 `i` loses ἑκών.** "against my will" carries the contrast with ἀέκοντα; adding "willingly" reads worse. Left.
- **7.224 note "στέρνοιο … a genitive of place with πρόσθε".** Loose but not false (πρόσθε takes the genitive). Left.
- **7.260 `l` "leaping upon him".** Supplies an object ἐπάλμενος leaves out; `i` and the note ("spring upon") are right. Left.
- **7.238 `i` "that is how I am able to fight on".** A reading of τό μοι ἔστι … πολεμίζειν, not a contradiction of `l`. Left.
- **7.231 `i` "there are men among us who could face you".** Recasts "we are such as"; recorded in new-renderings and sense-equal. Left.
- **7.186 `l` "had cast it into the helmet" (βάλε) and 7.217 "had challenged" (προκαλέσσατο).** Aorists in subordinate clauses rendered as pluperfects; the sequence demands it. Left.
- **7.214 καί in τὸν δὲ καὶ not rendered.** Weak "indeed"; `l` is already crowded. Left.
- **7.265 μέλανα "black" beside 7.262 μέλαν αἷμα "dark".** Matches the table's split (black of ships, night, death; dark of wine, water, wave, blood). Left.
- **7.258 note "as Ἀτρεΐδης is ‘Atreus’-son’".** The name is not in this part but the gloss is the table's. Left.
- **7.224 note "the other Ajax", 7.185 "the nine … previous part".** True of iliad-042 (the nine; the two Ajaxes). Left.
- **7.202 `l`/`i`, 7.201, 7.229–230 (Atreus' son dropped).** Compared with the published units character by character; identical except the capital at a unit's start and ";" for "·" at 7.230, as recorded.
- **Remembered English in `i`.** Read every `i` for phrases that arrived whole. The fixed ones ("bulwark of the Achaeans", "Zeus who gathers the clouds", "the black spirit of death", "lion-hearted", "bronze-shirted") are table rows. "stands his ground", "pounded", "yield to night" are plain English from the case relations. Nothing certain found beyond the 7.241 doubt above.
- **Scansion of other lines.** Only 251 was flagged; not re-scanned beyond it.
- **7.226 μετ’ Ἀχιλλῆα "next to him in rank".** Fair reading of μετά + acc.; left.

## For the caller

- **Decisions the drafter did not make that I did, and you may reverse:** (1) 7.269 takes the Iliad's "immeasurable" (5.245) over the Odyssey's "measureless" (9.538); to go the other way, revert `l`/`i`/`n` of 268 and drop the last new-renderings row. (2) 7.226 `i` is "all alone" because the 7.39 row says so; in this line the phrase means one man against one, and "all alone" may read as Hector alone; a note-level fix is already in the note, but the row could be re-examined. (3) 7.219 now follows the Odyssey's 17.71, but iliad-02x ships "came near" for ἐγγύθεν ἦλθον at 5.274 (not a table row); worth checking when the rows merge.
- **For the gloss pass:** parses to check against the line: ἔφαθ’ (ἔφατο elided, aspirated), ἔφαν (augmented), δίηται (middle subjunctive of δίεμαι), δείδιμεν (perfect, present sense), ἤλυθεν (augmented), πολεμήϊα (πολέμιος), νώροπι, ἐγχριμφθείς, ταλαύρινον, ἀπέλεθρον, ἱππότα, ἐνδέξια, ὑπέσχεθε, ἀπηνήναντο.

# Pass 2 — `gloss.json` and a re-read of `units.json`

`t` still untouched (checked again against the units before and after). `gloss.json` and `units.json` edited by script. Coverage checked: every form in `t` has an entry in the glossary, `novel-forms.json` or `known-forms.json`; the 135 keys of `gloss.json` are exactly the novel forms; every `__broaden__` value keeps the old entry whole before " · "; no entry is 230 characters or longer, none has an ASCII apostrophe or a backtick. Every novel parse and every known entry was read against the line.

Parses asked for, all checked against the line: ἔφαθ’ (known entry: ἔφατο elided, aspirated before οἳ — right), ἔφαν (known: impf./aor. 3 pl. — right), δίηται (pres. subj. mid. 3 sg. — right, matches the note; "general clause" wrong, fixed), δείδιμεν (perf. 1 pl., present sense — right), ἤλυθεν (aor. 3 sg., no claim about augment — right), πολεμήϊα (the broaden covers both lines: ἔργα, nom.; τεύχεα, acc. — right), νώροπι (dat. sg. agreeing with χαλκῷ — right; meaning fixed), ἐγχριμφθείς (aor. part. pass. with middle sense — right), ἀπέλεθρον (known entry "immeasurable", agrees with the new `l`/`i`), ταλαύρινον (a known form whose entry was masc. acc., "epithet of Ares"; this is a predicate neuter, so a reading was missing — added).

## Considered and refused in pass 2

- **Known entries τελαμώνιος "son of Telamon" and κορυθαίολος "glancing, flashing helmet".** Wording out of step with the table, but known entries are additions-only and the readings are not wrong in sense. Left; flagged.
- **ἐπομφάλιον "agreeing with σάκος or adverbial".** Both readings are given; the unit takes it as adverbial. Left.
- **ἐπάλμενος "’leaping on (them)’".** The object is the gloss's gloss only. Left.
- **βῶν "fem. acc. sg."** LSJ gives βοῦς both genders; ἀζαλέην agrees as feminine. Left.
- **ἔπεσον, ὑπήλυθε, ἐκσπασσαμένω, ἀναχασσάμενος, νήϊδά, ἑβδομάτῃ, μετέασι, ἀπέληγε, ἀνεκήκιεν, ἐγχείη, ἧκ, ἕσσατο.** Lemma, tense, person and case all right against the line.
- **Known ὃ, ὅς, ὃν, οἳ, ἣ, τὸν, τὼ, τῇ, τῷ, τῶν, οἱ, αὐτῷ, αὐτοῦ, γυῖα, μέσον, μακρὰ, ἂν, ἐπὶ, κατὰ.** Each use in this part falls under an existing reading (the possessive ἑὸν, the dual τὼ, ὃ μὲν … ὃ δ’, ἣ δὲ = "it", μακρὰ βιβάς are all covered).
